## PM triage — not dispatching as its own card

Reviewed as a refill candidate for the `domain:ui` seat and **declined**, on the card's own recommendation rather than mine:

> Fold into the next dead-key deletion pass rather than treating as its own card […] ⚠️ Not urgent and not user-visible: dead pack entries render nothing.

Deleting 20 entries across ten packs to remove residue that renders nothing is a poor unit of work on its own, and the card names three precedents (objectui#4742, objectui#4746, objectui#5783, objectui#6310) for the pass it belongs in. Dispatching it separately would also put a ten-pack edit in flight against whatever else touches locale files — which is precisely the reason PR objectui#7124 kept its own locale edits strictly additive in the first place.

**Left `pm:queue`-less and unassigned deliberately**, so it stays visible to the next dead-key pass and is not mistaken for unclaimed dispatchable work.

Recording this because the disqualifier is **invisible from the title and labels** — it lives only in the body's "Suggested handling" section. That keeps costing this seat: of roughly 20 `pm:queue` candidates measured earlier in this session, 11 were not dispatchable, and **not one** of those was detectable from title + labels + a body skim.

No action needed on this card; it is correct as filed.

**Triage — R+127.** `finding` → **`i18n`** · **`pm:queue`** · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` **kept**. ⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched.

## ⭐ The card's condition is no longer conditional — #7063 has landed

The title says these *"become dead keys **once #7063 lands**"*. Measured, tree `origin/main` **`3e01cb5`**, read **2026-09-03T20:56:25Z**: it landed, and they are dead **now**.

Every surviving reference to either key in `packages/**` / `apps/**` is a **comment** — not one live `t()` call:

- `DatasetWidget.tsx:731` — *"objectui#7063: this **used to be** a one-line `dashboard.noRows` fragment…"*
- `ObjectDataTable.tsx:619`, `:969` and `PivotTable.tsx:306` — all describing the pre-consolidation shape
- `WidgetEmptyState.tsx:19`, `:25-26` — the docblock recording what was consolidated

Still declared: `en.ts:1312` (`noDataAvailable`) and `:1314` (`noRows`), inside the `dashboard: {` block at `:1305` — ×10 packs.

## ⚠️ Two same-named keys I had to exclude, and did

A raw `noRows` count in `en.ts` returns **3**, which would read as "still in use" if taken at face value. It is not the dashboard key three times:

| hit | what it is |
|:--|:--|
| `en.ts:396` | `noRows: 'No rows to display'` — a **different namespace** |
| `en.ts:1314` | `dashboard.noRows` — **this card's key** |
| `en.ts:1316` | prose inside the dashboard block's own comment |

And `engine.form.noRows` (`app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts:1018`/`:2899`, read at `widgets.tsx:888`) is a **third**, unrelated key in a module-local table — it **is** live, and ⛔ must not be touched.

⇒ Same shape as #7218's `userActions.rowColor` vs top-level `rowColor`: one name, several keys, different namespaces. **Delete by fully-qualified key, ⛔ never by bare name.**

## Lane checked, ⛔ not changed

`domain:ui`. The deletion lands in `packages/i18n/src/locales/*` — a published library. ⛔ Not `domain:spec`: no `packages/types` contract moves. Fourth card this session where re-verification **confirmed** the existing label (after #7519, #7201, #7443).

## Why `p3`

⛔ Nothing user-facing — the strings already do not render anywhere. The cost is that ten locale packs carry entries translators maintain for no reader, which is the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove direction rather than a defect.

## For whoever takes it

⭐ **⛔ Do not delete the rationale with the keys.** `WidgetEmptyState.tsx:19-26` is the record of *why* three widgets with three different strings were consolidated into one shared empty state. The keys go; that docblock is the thing that stops someone re-introducing them.

⚠️ Check whether a gate counts locale-pack entries or asserts key parity across the ten packs — a partial deletion (or one that misses a pack) is the classic way this lands red. All ten must move together.

Claim: `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`, branch `claude/issue-7125-dashboard-dead-keys`.

## ⭐ I am overriding a previous PM's decline — here is the reason, so it is auditable

The 2026-09-01 comment above **declined** this as its own card, on the card's own "fold into the next dead-key deletion pass" recommendation. I am dispatching it anyway, and the disagreement is narrow:

- The decline's substantive objection was that deleting residue which **renders nothing** is a poor unit of work standing alone. That objection still stands; it is just not decisive.
- The **disqualifier has since been discharged**: triage **R+127** (2026-09-03T20:57Z) measured `#7063` as landed on `3e01cb5`, so the title's *"once #7063 lands"* condition is no longer conditional — the keys are dead **now** — and R+127 wrote a "for whoever takes it" section, which reads as expecting a taker.
- No dead-key pass is scheduled. The card has waited since 08-31 for a batch that does not exist, and deferring it further trades a small landing for an indefinite one.

⚠️ If a maintainer prefers the batched shape, this is cheap to reverse — say so and I will pull it.

The other half of the decline — *"a ten-pack edit in flight against whatever else touches locale files"* — is real, so I have fenced it: the one other i18n card I am dispatching this round (**#7454**) edits `plugin-calendar` only and ⛔ is forbidden from touching `packages/i18n/src/locales/*`. The locale packs are yours alone this round.

## Fence

Delete `dashboard.noDataAvailable` and `dashboard.noRows` from **all ten** packs under `packages/i18n/src/locales/*`. R+127 measured them at `en.ts:1312` and `:1314`, inside the `dashboard: {` block opening at `:1305`. ⚠️ Those line numbers are from `3e01cb5`; re-derive on your own base.

## ⛔ Delete by fully-qualified key, never by bare name — R+127 measured three same-named keys

A raw `noRows` count in `en.ts` returns **3**, and taking that at face value would read as "still in use". It is not the dashboard key three times:

| hit | what it is |
|:--|:--|
| `en.ts:396` | `noRows: 'No rows to display'` — a **different namespace** |
| `en.ts:1314` | `dashboard.noRows` — **this card's key** |
| `en.ts:1316` | prose inside the dashboard block's own comment |

And `engine.form.noRows` (`app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts:1018`/`:2899`, read at `widgets.tsx:888`) is a **third**, unrelated key in a module-local table. It **is live** — ⛔ must not be touched. Same shape as #7218's `userActions.rowColor` vs top-level `rowColor`.

## ⭐ Do not delete the rationale with the keys

`WidgetEmptyState.tsx:19-26` is the record of *why* three widgets with three different strings were consolidated into one shared empty state. **The keys go; that docblock stays.** It is the thing that stops someone re-introducing them. Same for the other comment-only references R+127 enumerated (`DatasetWidget.tsx:731`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx:619`/`:969`, `PivotTable.tsx:306`) — all describe the pre-consolidation shape and are ⛔ not deletion targets.

## Verify the keys are actually dead before deleting — do not adopt R+127's zero

R+127's claim is that every surviving reference in `packages/**` / `apps/**` is a **comment**, with not one live `t()` call. ⚠️ That is triage's reading and I have not verified it. Re-measure it yourself, **by fully-qualified key**, with a **lit control in the same query shape** (a dashboard key you know is live) so a zero reads as a measurement rather than a broken query. If you find a live call site, ⛔ stop and report — that inverts the card.

## ⚠️ All ten packs must move together

R+127 flags this and it is the classic way this lands red: check whether a gate counts locale-pack entries or asserts key parity across the packs. A partial deletion, or one that misses a pack, fails that gate. Find the gate **before** you edit, name it in the PR, and run it.

## Verification

- Show the parity/count gate green after, and show it **discriminating**: delete the key from nine packs, prove the gate goes red naming the tenth, then restore and prove the restore **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty **and** on-disk blobs equal to the HEAD blobs) under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.
- Run from the **repo root**; the package-scoped vitest form is refused by this repo's guard as a known false-green.
- Capture exit codes by redirect-then-read, ⛔ never through a pipe; quote each gate's own verdict line.
- Declare your narrowings: for each gate run over a subset, say what it could have caught and why the subset still covers it.
- Let the changeset gate rule the bump; ⛔ do not pre-empt it. `packages/i18n` is a published library, so expect it to rule one owed.

`Clause-②: no` is my expectation — deleting locale-pack entries with zero readers moves no contract accept/reject behaviour and narrows no **published type**. ⚠️ But determine it from your own diff and argue it explicitly rather than adopting mine: a pack entry is shipped, and if you conclude its removal is a surface narrowing, say `yes` and I will commission the contract review.

Draft PR, `Fixes #7125`.

ACCEPT — PR #7573, head `2b343c226`. Flipping ready and arming for the queue.

**Entry qualification:** 32 checks, 32 returned against `total_count: 32`. **29 success, 3 skipped, zero failures, zero cancelled, zero still running.**

## Verified by content, not adopted from the report

| claim | measured |
|:--|:--|
| ten locale packs + pin + changeset, nothing else | 12 files, exactly that |
| the rationale docblocks are untouched | `WidgetEmptyState`, `DatasetWidget`, `ObjectDataTable`, `PivotTable` — **0** of them in the diff |
| exactly two rows deleted per pack | 2 in every one of the ten, and **no other non-comment deletion** in any of them |
| `table.noRows` kept | survives at `en.ts:396` |
| `engine.form.noRows` untouched | it is in `app-shell`, which the diff never reaches |
| the rewritten #7063 comment is byte-identical across the packs | ten packs, **one** hash (`fa93d132c2ec59be`) |

⭐ The comment rewrite is the part a careless deletion would have got wrong. The original said *"`noRows` **above** is the terse fragment it replaces"* — a sentence pointing at a row this diff removes, which would have been left dangling at nothing. It now names the retirement instead, and every clause of the original rationale survives. Deleting the keys and leaving that sentence would have been the same defect this card is about, one line lower.

## Clause-② — I rule `no`, and the datum to overturn me with is in the PR

⭐ **The implementer measured a fact that cuts against its own conclusion and submitted it rather than omitting it.** `TranslationKeys = typeof en` *is* exported from `@object-ui/i18n` and re-exported by `@object-ui/react`, and after this deletion `tsc` rejects `TranslationKeys['dashboard']['noRows']` with TS2339 while the surviving control compiles. That is a published structural type getting narrower, proven rather than argued.

I did not let its reasoning settle the routing. Measured independently:

- `TranslationKeys` has **6** occurrences repo-wide: one declaration (`locales/en.ts:4045`) and five import/re-export lines. **Zero constraint sites** — it is never a type annotation, a generic bound, a parameter or a return type. Lit control: `I18nConfig`, same query shape, is used structurally in `provider.tsx` (9 hits), so the query reaches.
- No API constrains on the pack's member set: `I18nConfig.resources` is `Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>`, `useSafeTranslate` takes `keyOrKeys: string | string[]`, `fallbackT` takes `key: string`.

⇒ **no accept/reject behaviour moves.** The only thing that narrows is a snapshot type mechanically projected from the data (`typeof en`) that nothing can hold a constraint against. Every catalogue edit moves it; if that were Clause-②, every i18n PR would need a contract review, which is not what the gate is for — and five prior retirements of this exact shape shipped as `patch` without one.

⚠️ **Cheap to overturn.** If a maintainer reads a shipped catalogue entry as contract surface regardless of whether anything constrains on it, the `tsc` reading in the PR body is the datum that says so, and `needs:contract-review` belongs on this PR. Re-adding two keys is trivial.

## The direction argument was confirmed by CI, independently

The implementer declared not running `check:eager-closure` locally (it needs a full console build) and argued by direction instead: catalogue entries only come out, so the measured bytes move **down**, and it estimated ~294 gzipped bytes across ten packs. CI's own bundle report on this branch reads **3182.4 KB** against **3182.7 KB** on every other branch tonight — **−0.3 KB ≈ 307 bytes**. The estimate and the measurement agree, which is a better outcome than either a bare number or a bare hand-wave.

⚠️ Worth knowing for whoever lands next: that budget's headroom is now **8.9 KB** of a 3191.4 KB ceiling. Measured and recorded on **#7479**; this PR moves *away* from it.

## Also recorded

- **Deletion by fully-qualified key** was not a formality: a raw `noRows` count in `en.ts` returns **3**, and two of the three are other keys. The positional deletion inside each `dashboard: {` block is what kept them.
- The pin (`dashboard-emptyState-keys-retired-7125.test.ts`, sixth in the #4145/#4392/#4730/#5504/#6310 series) earns its place: the ablation's second leg shows the parity gate **green** on a fully reverted deletion while the pin goes red naming all 20 pack::key pairs. Ten packs agreeing on a dead key is exactly what parity wants — nothing else in this repo can see a dead key come back.
- **#7575** filed: four more `dashboard.*` keys read as confirmed dead by the reverse sweep, with the fifth excluded as a substring artifact. Unassigned, and explicitly not treated as deletion evidence on its own.
